method: Read the complete 12 final texts against the frozen facts and shared restrictions.
Check every recorded source/output excerpt for exact containment.
Distinguish asserted events from hypothetical explanations, general advice and arithmetic derived from supplied figures.
Record illustrative errors and qualifications; no binary human-quality pass rate.

summary.interpretation: Neutral briefs reduce explicit repeated advice labels in this sample, but do not prevent invented rules, events, participant details or unsupported inferences. Label absence does not mean no directive prose.

qualifications: All three fact sets are fictional, project-generated development inputs, not external human gold or a holdout.
Both brief variants request 650–900 words; shared length pressure was not independently varied. These observations cannot isolate its causal contribution.
The directed brief explicitly asks for repeated advice; complying with that structure is not itself a model failure.
Calculating 240−36 or an approximate 86/59 mean is not fabricated source data. Explicit hypotheticals about why books stay onsite or winter conditions are not counted as observed events.
The source says not to invent numbers; 100 minutes is therefore recorded as unsupported advice, not a fabricated historical duration.
The semantic issue counts are reviewer judgments, not a detector output or verified population error rate.
All 12 stopped normally; their short length is not an output truncation artifact.
